html: Ultraviolet rays can burn skin in minutes, and the damage adds up over the years as wrinkles, spots and a higher risk of skin cancer. Protection works best as a daily habit, even on cloudy days.

• Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen, SPF 30 or higher, and put more on every two hours or after swimming
  • Look for shade around midday
  • Wear a wide-brimmed hat, sunglasses and lightweight long sleeves
  • Skip tanning beds

section.sectionHead: Keep an eye on your skin
html: Show a clinician any spot that is new, changing or bleeding, or that simply looks different from your other moles.
